claim_ceiling: Known-truth fixture semantics only. No policy has been executed or scored. These cases do not demonstrate real-world economic effects.
evaluation_rule: The independent scorer may access oracle_facts. Candidate policies may access only policy_observation. Candidate code must not read oracle_facts.

cases.purpose: Prevent purchasing power or an allocation rule from manufacturing physical housing capacity.

constraints: No new build or conversion event occurs during the horizon.

invariants: No policy may house more households than the number of suitable units available or completed.
Any result claiming all three households housed is invalid unless it identifies an explicit capacity-changing event.

cases.purpose: Separate loan origination, construction progress, completion, and liability.
invariants: Loan origination and project approval do not increase safe housing capacity.
Capacity increases only after the modeled completion event.
The liability remains visible until a repayment, forgiveness, default, or other explicit liability event changes it.
No social-value or productivity conclusion follows from the financing event alone.

cases.purpose: Prevent public or philanthropic financing from being treated as costless.
invariants: A transfer changes the distribution of financial claims and purchasing power; it does not erase the physical resources consumed.
A planned renovation is not a completed renovation.
The grantor budget and recipient funding sides must reconcile under the selected accounting profile.

cases.purpose: Ensure stale or invalid inventory observations fail closed.
invariants: A stale listing cannot be promoted to current safe capacity without qualifying evidence.
Unknown or unverified safety status is not equivalent to safe or unsafe ground truth; candidate disposition must preserve uncertainty.

cases.purpose: Detect short-horizon strategies that improve current output by consuming future capacity.
invariants: Maintenance expense and future capacity loss must both appear in the outcome vector.
The skipped expense is not a net efficiency gain if it causes later service loss; any welfare valuation remains a declared policy choice.

cases.purpose: Distinguish internal reciprocal credit from externally spendable settlement assets.
invariants: Internal credit is not external purchasing power without a declared and funded conversion/settlement path.
No new capacity may be credited without the imported component or a documented substitute.

cases.purpose: Keep refinancing separate from net new financing and real investment.
invariants: New loan face value must not be reported as net new financing when proceeds repay predecessor debt.
Net new financing is not equivalent to new productive capacity without a separate evidenced use and production event.

cases.purpose: Separate payment incidence from physical expansion while leaving housing-service accounting to its own profile.
invariants: Payment is not evidence of new housing capacity.
The payment may correspond to a housing service under the declared national-account profile; do not infer that it is a net social gain, a net loss, or new construction from the payment alone.

cases.purpose: Prevent nominal unit totals from hiding capability-specific shortages.
invariants: The scorer must measure fit by declared capability requirements, not only total units.
An inaccessible unit must not be counted as satisfying a household's accessibility requirement.

cases.purpose: Prevent source count inflation when several records derive from the same original observation.
invariants: Mirrored claims with one source event are one provenance family for independence scoring.
Repeated or mirrored evidence cannot increase true available capacity.
